summary: ingest status cannot represent 'reviewed, awaiting your apply'
description:
The gates for nodes 11 and 14 test live/staged state only: "no pending
staged_tags rows" and "no pending staged_edges rows". Queued-but-unapplied
`review_actions` are invisible to them.

The flow deliberately separates review (agent or human) from apply (user
only). So the single most common intermediate state in the whole pipeline —
"every judgement is made and is sitting in the queue waiting for you" —
renders identically to "nobody has looked at this yet".

## Evidence

After the yoga-sutras node 14 pass, 696 edge verdicts were queued and
validated clean. `guru ingest status yoga-sutras-book-01` reported:

  [-] 14-edge-review    Curate the staged edges  ·gate
      nothing staged to review

Nothing distinguishes that from a text where node 13 has just run and no one
has started. Same for node 11 before the user applied: 2,579 queued verdicts,
status silent about all of them.

## Why it matters

1. It is the state the user needs to act on. The gate should be saying "696
   verdicts are waiting for POST /api/apply", which is a call to action, not
   an absence.
2. It makes agent hand-off reports unverifiable. A driver claiming "node 14
   complete" cannot be checked against the status machine, so the user has to
   take it on trust — which is exactly what the queue-then-apply design exists
   to avoid.
3. It hides queue-validation state. `scripts/validate_queue.py` knows whether
   the pending batch would apply cleanly; status does not surface it.

## Sketch

A third gate state between blocked and passed, e.g.

  [~] 14-edge-review    Curate the staged edges  ·gate
      696 verdicts queued (0 error, 0 warn) — awaiting your apply
      run: POST /api/apply   or   review with scripts/validate_queue.py -v

Requires status to count unapplied review_actions joined to this text's
staged_* rows, which is the same query validate_queue.py already runs.

Interacts with e9e17188: once status can see the queue, the reassign two-step
becomes legible too ("6 pending, all created by an applied reassign").
